title: Beat the (1-o(1)) log2 d exponent in quasi-polynomial polytope diameter bounds
premise_risks: arXiv:2609.33434 (Liu-Ge-Ye, 2026, unrefereed): the current best bound (n-d)^{log2 G_d}, G_d ~ (4 ln 2) d/(ln d)^2, and the claim that the leading term is sharp for path-counting recursions; recorded as context, Claim does not depend on it.
plain: All known bounds on the diameter of a d-dimensional polyhedron with n facets have the form (n−d)^{log₂ d − O(log log d)}. The latest (Liu–Ge–Ye 2026) is (n−d)^{log₂ G_d} with G_d ~ (4 ln 2) d/(ln d)². Get an exponent at most (1−ε) log₂ d.
math: Let $\Delta_u(d,n)$ be the maximum graph diameter of a pointed $d$-polyhedron with $n$ facets. Known: $\Delta_u(d,n)\le (n-d)^{\log_2 G_d}$, $G_d=(4\ln2+o(1))d/(\ln d)^2$ (Liu–Ge–Ye 2026), after Kalai–Kleitman, Todd, Sukegawa. Prove $\Delta_u(d,n)\le (n-d)^{(1-\varepsilon)\log_2 d}$ for some fixed $\varepsilon>0$ and all large $d$.
